title: The morning paper
desc: The back is the next day's tabloid front page. The headline is the whole story in three words (GROK NAILS IT / ACCENTURE FOOLS ALL FOUR / CLEAN SWEEP), the red deck gives the one number, three short sentences tell the pick, the bell and the verdict, and a box score keeps the four calls for anyone who wants them. Inverted pyramid: read the headline and stop, or read on.

title: Where they landed
desc: One picture tells it. A number line from up to down, each AI's call where it was made, the real move as the marker they were aiming at, and the gap from the nearest call drawn to scale: a hair-thin gold bar for Grok on Tesla, a long red one for Accenture. One line above sets it up (how they split), one line below says what happened. The fewest words of the four.

title: Fight night recap
desc: The round as a bout, in the site's fight-night voice. The AIs step into the bulls' or the bears' corner (an empty corner stays on the card: that is the story of Accenture and TSMC), the bell is the close, the decision says who won and by how much (by a hair, on points), and the belt is #1 on the board: the AI that makes the call on the next bet.

title: Three panels
desc: A comic strip, as Topps card backs carried a cartoon beside the numbers. The pick: four speech bubbles. The bell: the host holds up the close. The verdict: a burst with the number that matters and his reaction (stamping a win, a facepalm when nobody got it). The most charming, but it puts the host on every card back, against the one-host-per-tab rule.
